mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of periods with sustained HOUST increases, or HOUST growth does not correlate with other consumer demand indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO YoY decline does not correlate with other supply-side indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and CPIAUCSL YoY is below 2%, the real interest rate is high, signaling a restrictive monetary policy that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent monetary policy actions.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between UNRATE and PAYEMS does not correlate with wage inflation indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially during an expansionary regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of periods with sustained RSAFS increases during an expansionary regime, or RSAFS growth does not correlate with other consumer demand indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is growing faster than GDP (GDPC1) YoY, it signals a supply-side driven economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially in a late-cycle expansion.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO YoY growth > GDPC1 YoY growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction between INDPRO and GDPC1 does not correlate with other late-cycle indicators.
